note: Hand-verified corrections for item IDs that more than one source claims. Derived from the 2026-09-22 bundle (web/public/data/2026-09-22/items.bin and items.json), which ships 34,018 rows for 33,999 distinct IDs -- 19 IDs carried by two garments each. Each of those 19 duplicates was traced to two Fandom Clothing pages resolving to the same game ID because one of the two has a mistyped 'wardrobe nr' or 'type' in its infobox; six more (22414, 22576, 31367, 72361, 89667, 90846, found 2026-09-23) and 51204 (found 2026-09-25) are single wiki pages whose mistyped number or type lands on another garment's ID, clashing with every other source rather than with another page -- pipeline.CheckGarments, which holds every row against the packed table and Nikki Calc, now fails the build on any such row not listed here; the genuine owner of each ID was established independently from Nikki Calc's key list (ni-ids-v0.14.json + items-v0.14.json) and from the wiki's own item lists (the WIL entries on its Hairs, Dresses and other list pages), with the packed table's grades as a further check where it carries the garment, and a resolution is marked 'proven' only where Nikki Calc and the wiki's lists agree, or, where the wiki's list gives the number to both garments, Nikki Calc and the packed table's name and grades agree. correctIdForDropped is the dropped garment's real game ID where it could be established, 0 otherwise. RULE FOR THE PIPELINE: for each id listed under duplicates, take the row whose name does not match the ID's owner off that ID -- that is, keep 'keep' and discard 'drop' there, wherever the dropped garment appears -- and fail the build on any duplicate ID that is not listed here, so a new source error cannot pass silently. Where correctIdForDropped is given, the dropped row is read at that ID instead of discarded: in acquire.json always, and in the catalogue when that ID's slot is the row's own and the row's source has no other row there. A page whose mistyped field is 'type' states the wrong slot, so its catalogue row is still discarded and that ID keeps the other sources' row. An id listed under slotOverrides (none today) has its Item.Slot forced to 'slot' regardless of what the source's type field says: an override restores the slot the item's ID encodes and must also give the wearable place; where that place cannot be established the item is listed under excluded (none today) instead.

nameOverrides.name: Depicting Summer
nameOverrides.basis: Nikki Calc v0.14 (ni-ids-v0.14.json key A9121 -> items-v0.14.json name) gives 89121 = 'Depicting Summer'; the packed table (wardrobe.js) names 89121 夏季描绘 (Depicting Summer); the wiki's own Earrings list reads '{{WIL|9121|Depicting Summer}}'. Fandom page 'Memory of Summer' carries '|wardrobe nr = 9121', and page 'Depicting Summer' carries 9126: the two pages' numbers are swapped, and so are their 'how to obtain' fields, which follow the numbers. The page on 9121 says the Midsummer Festival event; that event's page lists Depicting Summer among its rewards, the suit page Summer Night Lavender lists it among the suit's parts, and the packed table has 89121 crafted like the suit's other event parts. So the page on 9121 carries 89121's number and how-to-obtain, while its title, caption and image belong to 89126. 89121 and 89126 have the same grades, slot and place in the wiki and the packed table, and the same rarity in Nikki Calc, so only the name changes.

nameOverridesNote: Wiki item pages whose title names another garment while everything else on the page describes the garment of the ID the page lands on. The ID keeps the page's row and the page's lines in acquire.json, under the name the other sources give that ID; wherever a row at that ID carries the page's title, it takes 'name' instead, and acquire.json reads the page under 'name' too, so other pages that name either garment point at the right ID.

displayNamesNote: Names shown in place of the one the sources give: where one source misspells a name or words it differently from the others, where the name is Nikki Calc's and the others give another (the entry's basis says why), where one source swaps the names of two items, and where a night form's name would be the wiki's page address ('/Night'): it shows the plain name, as the game does. 'was' is the name the build would show otherwise, after respacing; the build fails if the sources no longer give it. Only items.json and the acquire.json lines that print the name change: wiki pages, ingredients and suit parts are still matched by the sources' own spelling. A trailing bracket the wiki adds to tell items apart ('(Coat)', '(Hair)', '(Night)') is dropped from every shown name unless Nikki Calc's name carries the same bracket, since the game shows the plain name.

gradeOverridesNote: Grades kept against the wiki's item page where the packed table and Nikki Calc's sub-grade agree on another letter for the same attribute. 'grade' is the letter kept, 'was' the one the wiki gives; the build fails if the sources no longer give 'was' on that attribute.
